Sheet 21 shows behind-the-curb improvements along Collier Street including: (1) callout for 'PROPOSED VARIABLE WIDTH PUBLIC SIDEWALK EASEMENT', (2) numerous spot elevations prefixed with 'SW' (sidewalk) such as 'SW 549.20', 'SW 549.40', 'SW 549.00', and (3) a 'PROPOSED ADA PATH' shown by dotted line pattern per the legend, connecting down to the street level. Behind-the-curb improvements include sidewalks, pedestrian ramps, landscape strips, street trees, and lighting between the curb and property line. The grading plan sheet 21 explicitly shows proposed sidewalk improvements with a labeled public sidewalk easement, sidewalk spot elevations, and ADA paths along Collier Street. While not all behind-the-curb elements (trees, lighting) are detailed on the grading plan, the plan appropriately shows grading-related improvements and defers landscape details to landscape sheets per the notes.
findings.explanation: Behind-the-curb improvements shown on grading plan sheet 21, including proposed public sidewalk easement and ADA paths along Collier Street

findings.observation: Reviewed Grading Plan sheet 22. The legend explicitly defines two distinct contour line types: dashed lines labeled with numbers (e.g., '-- 535 --') represent 'EXISTING CONTOURS', and solid continuous lines with numbers in parentheses (e.g., '--(540)--') represent 'PROPOSED CONTOURS'. Visual examination of the plan confirms extensive use of both line types throughout the site. Existing contours (dashed lines labeled 536, 538, 540) are visible traversing the upper portion of the site, while proposed contours (solid lines labeled (542), (543), (544)) are concentrated around the proposed building footprint, driveways, and site boundaries. Spot elevations also use distinct symbols: 'x 533.00' for existing and '+ 533.00' for proposed.
findings.reasoning: The requirement is for a grading plan showing both existing and proposed grade lines. The grading plan sheets 21-22 clearly display both using standard civil engineering conventions with distinct line types defined in the legend. This allows contractors and reviewers to understand existing topography versus proposed grading changes. The sheets also include grade breaks, spot elevations, and flow arrows to fully communicate the grading design. Both existing and proposed grades are clearly distinguishable and comprehensively shown.
findings.explanation: Grading plan sheets 21-22 show both existing contours (dashed) and proposed contours (solid) with clear legend definitions

findings.observation: Reviewed the entire plan set including sheets 13 (Overall Site & Paving & Striping Plan), sheets 19-20 (Water & Wastewater Plan & Profile), sheets 25-26 (Storm Drain Plan), sheets 30-31 (Site Details), and all utility profile sheets. The plan shows TYPE II driveways connecting the site to existing streets (Collier Street and S Lamar Blvd), proposed sidewalks, and utility line extensions. Sheet 30 provides standard City of Austin details for TYPE II driveways, but these are driveway connections, not new roadways. Sheet 31 shows cross-sections for local streets but these are standard detail references, not proposed new roadway construction.
findings.reasoning: The condition for this item is 'If new roadway construction proposed'. A roadway is a public street designed for vehicular traffic, distinct from driveways or private access drives. The site plan shows site access via TYPE II driveways connecting to existing public streets, but no construction of new public roadways. The profile views in sheets 19-20 are for underground utilities, not roadway profiles. Since no new roadway construction is proposed, this checklist item does not apply to this project.
findings.explanation: No new roadway construction proposed; site access is via TYPE II driveway connections to existing streets

findings.observation: Reviewed the plan set for any indication of new roadway construction requiring target speed notation. As documented in CC-23-05, the plan shows TYPE II driveway connections to existing streets but no new public roadway construction. Sheets 13, 30, and 31 show paving, striping, and driveway details, but no roadway construction plans. No sheets contain target speed notations, which are required only for new or modified roadways per TCM guidance.
findings.reasoning: Per TCM, target speed is the intended design operating speed for a new roadway, distinct from posted speed limit. Target speed notation is required on roadway construction plans when new roadways are being built or existing roadways are being modified. Since this project proposes no new roadway construction (only driveway connections and sidewalks), there is no requirement for target speed notation. This item is conditional on new roadway construction, which is not present in this project.
findings.explanation: No new roadway construction proposed requiring target speed notation

However, 'signage and striping plan' in the context of item RDW-03 refers specifically to roadway signage and pavement striping (lane markings, arrows, stop bars, crosswalks) for new or modified roadways or streets within the ROW, not site paving or driveway apron striping. The TYPE II driveway connections are governed by standard City details (sheet 30) rather than custom signage/striping plans. Since no new roadway is being constructed or modified, signage and striping plans for roadway work are not applicable.
